These results indicate that cosmological hydrodynamic simulations, which heavily rely on supernova feedback to model how the early universe became transparent to ultraviolet light, may need reevaluation.

Published in Nature Communications, the findings demonstrate how Jupiter’s powerful magnetic environment manages high-energy solar particles differently than Earth, which relies on a simpler, single-frequency boundary. Because these plasma interactions share fundamental physics with extreme cosmic shocks found around supernova remnants, the observations provide a natural laboratory for studying energy dissipation in distant astrophysical environments.

Each block represents one meter, accurately replicating the country's topography, glaciers, lakes, and mountain peaks such as the Matterhorn using Minecraft Java Edition with the Cubic Chunks mod.

Available in early access, the full 24-gigabyte world requires a high-performance computer with at least 16 gigabytes of RAM and is priced at 15 Swiss francs for residents of Switzerland, while a free regional download featuring the Jungfrau-Aletsch UNESCO World Heritage site is provided for hardware testing. The map utilizes swisstopo vector and raster datasets for domestic terrain and infrastructure, supplemented by Copernicus elevation data for areas beyond national borders.

entry.title: Merck and Moderna Announce Phase 3 Trial Results for Intismeran Melanoma Vaccine
entry.content:
Links: arstechnica.com | source | hacker news

Merck and Moderna have released detailed Phase 3 trial results showing that their personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, intismeran, combined with the immunotherapy drug Keytruda, reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42 percent compared to Keytruda and a placebo. The trial evaluated patients with resected melanoma over a two-year period, tracking both recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival.

The therapy uses synthetic mRNA coded for up to 34 patient-specific mutations identified by comparing cancer cells to healthy tissue, triggering a targeted immune response. While the two-year treatment effect was slightly lower than milestones observed in earlier phase-two data, researchers describe the findings as a significant clinical advance and the first Phase 3 study to demonstrate meaningful improvements over standard-of-care Keytruda in this setting.
